alwalkeria:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: Other archosaur research)

facts.statement: The genus Alwalkeria was first described by Sankar Chatterjee in 1987.
facts.quote: authority: (Chatterjee, 1987)

facts.statement: The original name Walkeria was rejected because it was preoccupied by a bryozoan.
facts.quote: synonyms: Walkeria Chatterjee, 1987 (preoccupied)

facts.statement: The replacement name Alwalkeria was proposed in 1994 by Chatterjee and Creisler.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Chatterjee & Creisler, 1994

facts.statement: Alwalkeria is an extinct avemetatarsalian genus known from the Late Triassic Lower Maleri Formation of India.
facts.quote: Alwalkeria (; "for Alick Walker") is a historically problematic extinct genus of avemetatarsalian known from the Late Triassic Lower Maleri Formation of India.

facts.statement: Early research interpreted the fossils as belonging to a podokesaurid theropod, a herrerasaur, or an Eoraptor-like basal eusaurischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Early research interpreted the material belonging to a 'podokesaurid' (coelophysoid) theropod, herrerasaur, or Eoraptor-like basal eusaurischian dinosaur.

facts.statement: Subsequent work determined that the fossils referred to this species are chimeric, belonging to multiple unrelated taxa.
facts.quote: Subsequent work recognized the chimaeric status of the fossils referred to this species, as they belong to multiple unrelated taxa.

facts.statement: In 1987, Chatterjee named Walkeria maleriensis based on specimen ISI R 306, containing a partial skull, around 28 vertebrae, femur fragments, and an astragalus.
facts.quote: In 1987, Sankar Chatterjee named Walkeria maleriensis as a new genus and species of podokesaurid theropod dinosaurs based on specimen ISI R 306, which includes a partial skull, around 28 vertebrae, a proximal left femur, a distal right femur, and an astragalus (ankle bone).

facts.statement: The specimen was recovered from the Godavari Valley locality in the Maleri Formation of Andhra Pradesh, India.
facts.quote: The specimen was recovered in the Godavari Valley locality from the Maleri Formation of Andhra Pradesh, India.

facts.statement: The remains were collected in 1974 from red mudstone deposited during the Carnian stage, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: The remains were collected by Chatterjee in 1974 in red mudstone that was deposited during the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago.

facts.statement: The specimen is housed in the collection of the Indian Statistical Institute in Kolkata, India.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the collection of the Indian Statistical Institute, in Kolkata, India.

facts.statement: The specific name maleriensis refers to the Lower Maleri Formation in southern India where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name, maleriensis, is a reference to the Lower Maleri Formation, in southern India, where its fossils were found.

facts.statement: Chatterjee originally described the taxon as a basal theropod.
facts.quote: Chatterjee described the taxon as a basal theropod.

facts.statement: Paul (1988) assigned Alwalkeria to Herrerasauridae based on femur features.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) understood Alwalkeria as a link between herrerasaurids and the genus Protoavis, and hence assigned it to Herrerasauridae based on features of the femur.

facts.statement: Langer (2004) and Martínez and Alcober (2009) considered Alwalkeria too primitive to be a theropod and classified it as a basal saurischian.
facts.quote: However, Langer (2004) and Martínez and Alcober (2009), observed that Alwalkeria was too primitive to be a theropod and considered it a basal saurischian.

facts.statement: In 2005, Rauhut and Remes found Alwalkeria to be a chimera with a crurotarsan skull and dinosaurian femur and astragalus.
facts.quote: In 2005, Rauhut and Remes found Alwalkeria to be a chimera, with the anterior skull referable to a crurotarsan, and the vertebrae referable to various other ancient reptiles including Prolacertiformes; however, they claimed the femur and the astragalus were clearly dinosaurian, with the latter possessing saurischian characteristics.

facts.statement: In 2011, Novas and colleagues argued Alwalkeria remains valid based on femur and astragalus morphology similar to basal dinosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2011, Novas and colleagues argued that Alwalkeria remains valid on the basis of an unusual morphology of its femur and an astragalus with a conservative morphology more similar to that of basal dinosaurs.

facts.statement: In 2016, Lecuona, Ezcurra, and Irmis reiterated the chimeric nature of the holotype, noting the skull could belong to Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: In 2016, Lecuona, Ezcurra & Irmis reiterated the chimaeric nature of the Alwalkeria holotype, noting that the skull material could be referred to the Crocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: McDavid, Marchant, and Reid suggested Alwalkeria can only be confidently assigned to Pan-Aves incertae sedis, not a lagerpetid.
facts.quote: They agreed with restricting the holotype of Alwalkeria to ISI R 306b, the distal femur, but suggested that the taxon can only be confidently assigned to Pan-Aves (=Avemetatarsalia) incertae sedis, not a lagerpetid pterosauromorph as proposed by Sen & Ray (2025).

facts.statement: Alwalkeria lived during the Late Triassic in the Lower Maleri Formation of India.
facts.quote: Alwalkeria (; "for Alick Walker") is a historically problematic extinct genus of avemetatarsalian known from the Late Triassic Lower Maleri Formation of India.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Carnian stage of the Triassic, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: The remains were collected by Chatterjee in 1974 in red mudstone that was deposited during the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria lived at the end of the Triassic, approximately 220 million years ago, during the Carnian stage in what is now the Indian subcontinent.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del Triásico, hace aproximadamente 220 millones de años, durante el Carniense, en lo que es hoy el subcontinente indio.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria was a small omnivorous dinosaur, estimated to reach about one meter in length.
facts.quote: Alwalkeria fue un pequeño dinosaurio omnívoro, por la escasez de fósiles no se sabe cuanto medía y pesaba, aunque se calcula que solo llegaba al metro de largo.

facts.statement: The partial skull measures approximately 4 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El Cráneo parcial mide aproximadamente 4 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest Alwalkeria may have reached only 50 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Estimaciones han sugerido que Alwalkeria habría alcanzado los 50 cm de largo.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated a weight of 2 kilograms and a length of 1.5 meters in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó por su parte un peso de 2 kilogramos y un largo de 1,5 metros en 2010.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria possessed heterodont dentition in the upper jaw, with teeth varying in shape based on their position.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio también tiene una dentición heterodonta en la mandíbula superior, los dientes tiene diferente forma según la posición que ocupan dentro e la boca.

facts.statement: Like Eoraptor and basal sauropodomorphs, Alwalkeria had thin, straight front teeth and backward-curving side teeth, though none were serrated.
facts.quote: Al igual a Eoraptor y a los sauropodomórfos basales, los dientes delanteros son delgados y rectos, mientras que los dientes en los lados de la quijada se curvan hacia atrás como los de los terópodos predadores, aunque ninguno esta aserrado.

facts.statement: This dental arrangement suggests Alwalkeria was an omnivore with a varied diet including insects, small vertebrates, and plants.
facts.quote: Esta disposición dental no es ni claramente herbívoro ni claramente carnívoro, que sugiere que este dinosaurio fuera un omnívoro con una dieta variada, incluyendo insectos, pequeños vertebrados, y vegetales.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria is unique among basal dinosaurs for its teeth without denticles and a proportionally wider mandibular symphysis than almost any other known dinosaur.
facts.quote: Varias características hacen Alwalkeria único entre dinosaurios basales. Además de sus dientes sin dentículos, y una sínfisis de la mandíbula proporcional más ancha que casi cualquier otro dinosaurio conocido.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria also possessed a very large articulation between the perone and the ankle.
facts.quote: También, tiene una articulación muy grande entre el peroné y el tobillo.

facts.statement: The fossil remains may belong to a juvenile individual, consisting of anterior jaw fragments, 28 incomplete vertebrae, most of a femur, an astragalus, and a partial skull.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de este dinosaurio quizá eran de un ejemplar juvenil, se halló un espécimen conocido por las el extremo anterior de la mandíbulas superiores e inferiores, 28 vértebras incompletas de todas las partes de su columna vertebral, la mayor parte de un fémur, y un astrágalo y un cráneo parcial que es de aproximadamente 4 centímetros.

facts.statement: Subsequent work recognized the chimeric status of the fossils, indicating they belong to multiple unrelated taxa.
facts.quote: Subsequent work recognized the chimaeric status of the fossils referred to this species, as they belong to multiple unrelated taxa.

facts.statement: Some bones may belong to a dinosaur, while the skull is likely from a pseudosuchian.
facts.quote: Some of the bones may belong to a dinosaur, and the skull is likely from a pseudosuchian.

facts.statement: A 2025 review regarded A. maleriensis as a member of Pan-Aves (Avemetatarsalia) of uncertain placement.
facts.quote: A 2025 study suggested lagerpetid affinities for the femora, though this was deemed unlikely by a subsequent review, which regarded A. maleriensis as a member of Pan-Aves (Avemetatarsalia) of uncertain placement.

facts.statement: Researchers identified the distal femur as an indeterminate representative of the pseudosuchian clade.
facts.quote: They also observed that the distal femur was more consistent with the morphology of pseudosuchians, leading them to identify this bone fragment as an indeterminate representative of that clade.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria is classified within the superorder Dinosauria.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria

facts.statement: Alwalkeria is tentatively classified within the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia?

facts.statement: It is debated whether Alwalkeria belongs to a podokesaurid theropod, a herrerasaur, or an Eoraptor-like basal eusaurischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Early research interpreted the material belonging to a 'podokesaurid' (coelophysoid) theropod, herrerasaur, or Eoraptor-like basal eusaurischian dinosaur.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Alwalkeria is a theropod or a basal saurischian.
facts.quote: However, Langer (2004) and Martínez and Alcober (2009), observed that Alwalkeria was too primitive to be a theropod and considered it a basal saurischian.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the skull material belongs to a dinosaur or a crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: In 2016, Lecuona, Ezcurra & Irmis reiterated the chimaeric nature of the Alwalkeria holotype, noting that the skull material could be referred to the Crocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the femora belong to a novel lagerpetid named Alickmeron maleriensis or to Alwalkeria.
facts.quote: In 2025, Sen & Ray determined the partial femora belonged to a novel representative of the Lagerpetidae, which they named Alickmeron maleriensis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Alwalkeria should be assigned to Pan-Aves incertae sedis or to the lagerpetid clade.
facts.quote: They agreed with restricting the holotype of Alwalkeria to ISI R 306b, the distal femur, but suggested that the taxon can only be confidently assigned to Pan-Aves (=Avemetatarsalia) incertae sedis, not a lagerpetid pterosauromorph as proposed by Sen & Ray (2025).

facts.statement: Alwalkeria was originally described by Chatterjee in 1987 as a basal theropod.
facts.quote: Chatterjee en 1987 describió originalmente a Alwalkeria como un terópodo basal.

facts.statement: In 1998, Paul classified Alwalkeria as a link between herrerasaurids and the genus Protoavis, assigning it to Herrerasauridae based on femur characteristics.
facts.quote: En 1998, Paul ve a Alwalkeria como un enlace entre los herrerasáuridos y del género Protoavis y por lo tanto asignado a Herrerasauridae basado en las características del fémur.

facts.statement: Langer in 1994 and Martínez and Alcober in 2009 argued that Alwalkeria was too primitive to be a theropod and considered it a basal saurischian.
facts.quote: Sin embargo Langer en 1994 y Martínez y Alcober en 2009, observaron que Alwalkeria era demasiado primitivo para ser un terópodo y la consideraban un saurisquio basal.

facts.statement: The current scientific consensus is that this genus occupies a basal position within Saurischia.
facts.quote: El consenso científico actual es que este género de hecho ocupan una basales posición dentro Saurischia.

facts.statement: Rauhut and Remes in 2005 hypothesized that Alwalkeria was a chimera, with the anterior skull part belonging to a crurotarsian and the vertebrae belonging to other ancient reptiles.
facts.quote: Rauhut & Remes (2005) encontraron que Alwalkeria sería una quimera, con la parte anterior del cráneo perteneciente a crurotarsiano, y las vértebras pertenecientes a otros antiguos reptiles.

facts.statement: The femur and astragalus are clearly dinosaurian, possessing characteristics of saurischians.
facts.quote: El fémur y el astrágalo son claramente dinosaurianos, poseyendo características de saurisquios.

facts.statement: Alwalkeria is classified within the parent group Saurischia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saurischia

facts.statement: Alwalkeria lived during the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Alwalkeria in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: McDavid, Marchant, and Reid in 2026 revised the nomenclature of Alickmeron maleriensis, considering it a junior objective synonym of Alwalkeria maleriensis and reinterpreting it as an indeterminate member of Pan-Aves.
facts.quote: McDavid, Marchant, & Reid (2026) revise the nomenclature of Alickmeron maleriensis and consider it a junior objective synonym of Alwalkeria maleriensis due to being based on the same holotype and type species, also reinterpreting it as an indeterminate member of Pan-Aves.
